messages:
Jia: heads up — after landing tokenizer v2 + int4 quant build for q4b-lite we see a weird uptick in dedupe hits for the prompt bank and a small short-prompt quality regression in the eval set. not sure if it's tokenization mismatch or a quant artifact.

Marco: can you paste the quick numbers? is this duplication in ingestion or during offline dedupe pass? :thinking_face: 

Jia: quick snapshot from the staging run:
```
ingest_total=128k
dedupe_before_tokenizer_v2=0.9% duplicates
dedupe_after_tokenizer_v2=7.3% duplicates
short_prompt_f1_drop=+4.8% absolute (on small-chat benchmark)
```
All runs used the same fingerprinting hash but tokenizer change altered tokenization boundaries for a subset of samples.

Riya: that jump is big. could also explain the f1 hit if many short prompts now split/pad differently and trigger different model behavior after quantization. did you rerun a token-level diff between v1 and v2 for the sample subset?

Jia: small diff done — ~18k prompts changed token boundaries. I attached a short example: "What's the time?" -> v1 tokens 3, v2 tokens 5 (adds punctuation tokens). Many of these are small conversational prompts.

Sam: hmm. two axes to consider: 1) dedupe pipeline fingerprint should be tokenizer-agnostic (hash on normalized text) OR we need a tokenizer-stable fingerprint step; 2) quantization may amplify small context shifts, so we should isolate whether the quality regression is from tokenization or int4.

CI-bot: deploy ci/quant4b-int4-tokenizer_v2 completed — unit tests: 214 passed, 3 skipped, 2 flaky flagged. See: https://ci.redwood/334455

Marco: proposal: revert only tokenizer for a quick A/B on staging (keep int4), and run a targeted diff on the 18k changed prompts with the int4 model. If regression disappears with v1 tokenizer, it's tokenizer. If not, quant. Also run dedupe with normalized-to-utf8 pre-tokenizer to see if duplicate rate drops.

Riya: agree. I can spin the dedupe run with normalization and relaxed windowing (merge tokens across punctuation) — should be fast. If that reduces duplicates to ~1% we have a path: update fingerprinting to use normalized text + short-token canonicalization.

Jia: timeline: I'll trigger tokenizer rollback A/B now (staging group) and collect the eval traces for the 18k subset. Riya — if you can run the normalized dedupe in parallel that'd be great. Sam — can you prepare a tiny param sweep for int4 scale/zero-point settings we can run if we conclude quant is the culprit?

Sam: on it. I'll prepare 3 sweep configs and a minimal harness to run only the changed set (should finish in ~90m).

Riya: kicked off dedupe-normalized job (job id dedupe-334455). ETA ~40min.

Jia: thanks — ping here when the A/B is done. if dedupe-normalized fixes the dup rate, we should patch the fingerprinter and run a fast migration on the ingest queue rather than revert. Otherwise we'll need to coordinate a model/quant rollback plan.

Marco: and please snapshot a few raw examples that went from unique->duplicate after v2 so labeling team can sanity-check. we may need to prioritize relabeling for those that are now marked duplicates but are actually distinct intents.

Jia: noted — dumping 200 sample ids to the thread when available.

CI-bot: dedupe-334455 finished: normalized dedupe duplicates=1.1% (reduced from 7.3%). Results at https://ci.redwood/334455/dedupe-report

Riya: nice! sounds like fingerprinting was the main driver. next steps: patch fingerprinter to run normalization + short-token canonicalization, create migration job for queued items, and schedule a small relabel batch to validate edge cases.

Sam: still going to run the int4 sweep in case we want to tighten quant settings later — launching now.

Jia: awesome — closing loop: I'll open a short RFC for the fingerprint change and migration plan, and drop the sample dump in ~10m. thanks all :raised_hands:
